meta.name: Hesperia, 1890
meta.description: An invented world of two continents facing each other across the Narrows: the old Empire of Varr and its rival kingdoms in the west, the lowland workshops of Lys, the forests of Kharsk and the ancient Tessarine plateau in the east, an island kingdom in the ocean and planters’ isles in the south. Three frontiers start unclaimed: the frozen Hoarlands, the Red Waste and the outer Sapphire Isles.
meta.blurb: A large original campaign: about 700 provinces and 22 realms on two continents, with crossings, frontiers and an island sea power.
meta.style: Two continents across a narrow sea
attribution: Geography, realms and names authored for Crown & Frontier (tools/hesperia.data.ts); the towns’ names are drawn from the game’s naming cultures.

nations.name: Empire of Varr
nations.summary: The old empire of the Saune plain, master of the largest army in the west and of the lakes at its heart, hemmed in by the kingdoms it once ruled.
nations.strength: A rich heartland and a deep reserve of men.
nations.constraint: Neighbours on every side remember its rule.

nations.name: Kingdom of Skarholt
nations.summary: A kingdom of fjords and fells on the cold north coast of Varr, with the Skerries offshore and the timber of the whole north.
nations.strength: Seafarers: straits cost less to cross and trade pays more.
nations.constraint: Thin soil and long winters.

nations.name: Kingdom of Morvaine
nations.summary: A highland crown on the Bay of Sorrows, whose glens have never been held by an outsider for long.
nations.strength: Highland forts: forts cost less and defenders hold.
nations.constraint: Poor and remote.

nations.name: Confederacy of the Ironspine
nations.summary: Mining cantons along the western mountains, armed and neutral, selling iron to every side.
nations.strength: Iron and militia: iron is cheap and the passes are held.
nations.constraint: No plain to feed an army.

nations.name: Grand Duchy of Velland
nations.summary: A wealthy duchy of dykes and harbours on the Narrows, a buffer between Varr and the eastern kingdoms.
nations.strength: Commerce and good relations.
nations.constraint: Flat, small and coveted.

nations.name: Most Serene Republic of Lorresse
nations.summary: The merchant republic of the Saune delta, whose banks lend to half the crowns of Varr and whose fleet guards the southern mouth of the Narrows.
nations.strength: Banking and shipping: trade and income above its size.
nations.constraint: Few men for a great fleet.

nations.name: Kingdom of Aster
nations.summary: A sun-dried kingdom of vineyards and hill towns between the Saune and the Ironspine, rival of Lorresse and old vassal of Varr.
nations.strength: Hardy hill soldiers.
nations.constraint: Little industry and rich neighbours.

nations.name: Holy See of Saint Ilse
nations.summary: The seat of the faith of the west, a small sacred realm whose word still moves kings.
nations.strength: Its word carries: others think well of it and envoys go further.
nations.constraint: A tiny army in the middle of the great powers.

nations.name: Sultanate of Qasreen
nations.summary: A desert sultanate on the dry southern peninsula of Varr, horse-breeders and caravan lords who covet the vineyards to the north.
nations.strength: Desert horsemen: cavalry strikes hard and costs less.
nations.constraint: Dry land: food and industry are scarce.

nations.name: Kingdom of Corwen
nations.summary: An island kingdom in the western ocean, with the strongest fleet in Hesperia and a habit of keeping the continent divided.
nations.strength: The sea: trade pays more and fleets are cheap.
nations.constraint: A small army that must cross the sea.

nations.name: Lordship of Hask
nations.summary: A rock in the middle of the Narrows whose lords take tolls from every ship between the two continents.
nations.strength: Tolls and pilots: trade pays and straits are cheap.
nations.constraint: One island and many covetous neighbours.

nations.name: Kingdom of Lys
nations.summary: The lowland kingdom on the eastern shore of the Narrows, crowded with mills and canals, the workshop of Ostmere.
nations.strength: Industry and canals: factories and research above its size.
nations.constraint: Low, flat and open to invasion.

nations.name: Free City of Halden
nations.summary: The free city at the Needle, the narrowest crossing between the continents, whose guarantee every great power has signed.
nations.strength: The crossing: trade pays and others respect it.
nations.constraint: One city between two worlds.

nations.name: Electorate of Brennholt
nations.summary: A forest electorate behind the Greywall, with coal in its hills and a staff college that trains the officers of half the east.
nations.strength: Staff work: research is quick and forts cheap.
nations.constraint: Between Lys, Kharsk and Doros.

nations.name: Tsardom of Kharsk
nations.summary: The vast tsardom of the northern forests and the eastern plains, slow to stir and impossible to exhaust.
nations.strength: Endless manpower: armies are cheap to fill.
nations.constraint: Few railways: supply and research are slow.

nations.name: Kingdom of Doros
nations.summary: A young kingdom between the Eagle Ridge and the Kharsk forests, freed from the Tessarine Empire within living memory and eager for more.
nations.strength: Veterans: soldiers fight well.
nations.constraint: Surrounded by larger realms.

nations.name: Tessarine Empire
nations.summary: The ancient empire of the high plateau, ringed by the Crown Mountains, whose provinces have been falling away for a century.
nations.strength: The plateau: defenders fight well at home and forts are cheap.
nations.constraint: Debts and restless provinces.

nations.name: Principality of Oskel
nations.summary: A coastal principality of olive groves and ports under the western wall of the Crown Mountains.
nations.strength: Ports and orchards.
nations.constraint: Between the plateau and the sea.

nations.name: Horde of Tarkhan
nations.summary: The horse-lords of the eastern steppe, who have raided the plateau and the Kharsk frontier for six hundred years.
nations.strength: Horsemen: cavalry strikes hard and costs less.
nations.constraint: No towns to speak of: little income or research.

nations.name: Khedivate of Amun
nations.summary: The river kingdom of the Amun valley, green between two deserts, nominally a province of the Tessarine Empire and in fact its own master.
nations.strength: The river: food and population grow.
nations.constraint: Deserts on both sides.

nations.name: Emirate of Sahrun
nations.summary: An emirate of oases and caravan roads on the southern edge of the Red Waste, rich in nitrates and poor in everything else.
nations.strength: Desert warfare: soldiers fight well in the waste.
nations.constraint: Thin land and few people.

nations.name: Republic of Sapphira
nations.summary: A planters’ republic on the Great Sapphire, the richest of the southern isles, with unclaimed islands all around it.
nations.strength: Plantations and ships: trade pays well.
nations.constraint: A small island far from everyone.
